correctness.rationale: The exact short-step identities were reconstructed. With \(n=ux^2\), one curvature-matched step gives \(x^+=x(1+2n-2x^2/a)\) and \(n^+=x^4(4/a-4u)+O(x^6)\); an independent symbolic expansion reproduces these coefficients exactly. A second short step therefore resets the leading normal coefficient to \(4/a\). At a pre-Polyak state \(n=cx^4+O(x^6)\), expanding the exact Polyak step gives \(X=3x/4+O(x^3)\) and \(N=(7/16-ac/8)x^2+O(x^4)\); substituting \(c=4/a\) returns to a bounded parabolic wedge and yields the Q-factor. With one short step, \(c=4/a-4u+O(x^2)\), hence the affine multiplier \(8a/9\) and the threshold \(a=9/8\). The summable \(O(x_m^2)\) perturbation closes the attracting case.
correctness.risk: The theorem is local and tied to \(h=1/(2a)\); the one-step threshold is for the scaled normal mode, not a global convergence iff.

final_claim: For the quartic Rosenbrock family \(f_a(x,y)=x^4+a(y-x^2)^2\) with curvature-matched short step \(h=1/(2a)\), two short gradient steps followed by one Polyak step have local Q-linear factor \(3/4\) for every \(a>0\); with one short step the scaled normal coordinate obeys \(u_{m+1}=(8a/9)u_m-1/9+O(x_m^2)\), so its sharp attraction threshold is \(a<9/8\).
limitations: The theorem does not claim global convergence or optimality of the chosen short stepsize.
Numerical replay is supporting evidence only.
